argument_summary: Certification is supportable only on a monitored, explicitly caveated basis. The admissible record shows aggregate launch readiness above threshold by 2.4 percentage points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports deployment readiness at the overall release level. The same record also shows a below-target named launch use-case issue in health-plan benefits support, concentrated in benefits-eligibility explanation, plus a draft runbook that does not yet satisfy the policy standard for removing disclosure obligations. The narrow defensible position is therefore certification with recorded limitations, disclosure, and follow-up mitigation completion, not a clean certification finding.
claims_about_business_cost: No policy claim should depend on business cost. The appropriate governance outcome can still avoid unnecessary escalation because the admissible evidence supports a bounded, monitored release posture rather than a finding that blocks certification outright.
claims_about_policy: The policy text says certification without material caveats requires current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. That standard is not met here because the remaining launch use-case weakness is still present and the runbook is still draft. Public risk-management guidance supports deployment with measurement and monitoring, and model-card guidance supports documenting limitations and evaluation results. On this record, policy is best satisfied through caveated certification with explicit disclosure rather than escalation to a cleaner compliance claim.
concessions: The health-plan benefits support slice remains below target, concentrated in benefits-eligibility explanation.
The draft runbook does not yet include a fully resolved governance structure sufficient to remove the disclosure issue.
The model-card record is not clean because the current draft says there are no known material limitations while reviewer comments already raise whether this issue must be disclosed.
